newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra still finalising Telstra sale timing.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra still finalising Telstra sale timing.

text.p: Australian Finance Minister John Fahey said on Wednesday the government was still to finalise the timing for the one-third sale of telecoms carrier Telstra Corp.
"Given the significant preparatory and planning steps necessary for the partial sale of Telstra, a final decision on timing has not yet been made," Fahey said in a statement.
The first stage of the partial sale process was to co-ordinate the selection of government advisers to assist with the necessary planning, he said.
The government plans to raise about A$8.0 billion through the sale.

Fahey said he would decide specific sale issues such as the offer structure, taking into account advice from the government's professional advisers as well as the results of the recently established Senate inquiry.
The Senate is the upper house of parliament.
He said the office of asset sales would oversee the sale process.

Legislation for the sale of one-third of Telstra was passed in the Senate last week, but analysts have said the sale is not expected to take place until the final quarter of calendar 1997. -- Canberra Bureau 61-6 273-2730
